form.title: IB Diploma Year 2 Science onboarding test

writes.rule: Per subtopic seen: pMastery 0.7 if right at D2/D3, 0.55 if right at D1, 0.25 if wrong; level L0-L3 from the ladder step reached
Prerequisite-gap index = 100 x weighted misses / weighted items seen in slots 1-4, averaged over groups
Groups with the highest Part A percent (top 1-2, only if >= 65%)
Groups with the lowest Part A percent (bottom 1-2, only if < 65%)
Calibration = 1 - mean |confidence/5 - correct| over Part A (feeds the first MCI reading)
Highest difficulty answered correctly twice in a row: D1 low, D2 medium, D3 high
Verbal reasoning = percent of Part B verbal items right
Numerical reasoning = percent of Part B numerical items right
Abstract reasoning = percent of Part B abstract items right
Spatial reasoning = percent of Part B spatial items right
Logical deduction = percent right on Part B items tagged p65
Numeracy fluency = numerical percent scaled by speed (right answers under target time count 1.2x, max 100)
Processing speed = 100 x share of Part B items answered right within target seconds
RIASEC profile: each career-interest item scored 1-5; letter score = mean of its 2 items; top 3 letters form the code (e.g. IRC)

items.stem: A 1 kg ball at 6 m/s hits a stationary 2 kg ball and they move off together. What is their speed?
items.markingKey: D. 2 m/s. Momentum 6 = 3v

items.stem: Work done by a force equals
items.answer: force x distance moved in the direction of the force
options: force x distance moved in the direction of the force
items.markingKey: A. force x distance moved in the direction of the force. W = Fs

items.stem: A 50 kg student climbs 4 m of stairs in 5 s. What is the useful power? (g = 10 N/kg)
For a projectile, ignoring air resistance, the horizontal velocity
items.markingKey: D. stays constant. No horizontal force

items.stem: An object moves in a circle at constant speed. Its acceleration is
items.answer: towards the centre of the circle
options: towards the centre of the circle
items.markingKey: C. towards the centre of the circle. Centripetal acceleration

items.stem: A ball is thrown horizontally at 10 m/s from a 20 m high cliff. How far from the base does it land? (g = 10 m/s²)
items.markingKey: B. 20 m. Fall time √(2 x 20 ÷ 10) = 2 s, then 10 x 2

items.stem: The time for one complete oscillation is the
items.markingKey: D. period. T = 1/f

items.stem: A pendulum makes 20 oscillations in 10 s. What is its frequency?
In simple harmonic motion, where is the speed of the oscillator greatest?
items.markingKey: D. At the equilibrium position. All energy is kinetic at the centre

items.stem: Like charges
options: have no effect on each other
items.markingKey: A. repel each other. Basic electrostatics

items.stem: If the distance between two point charges is doubled, the force between them becomes
items.markingKey: A. one quarter as large. Inverse square law

items.stem: What is the field strength between parallel plates 0.02 m apart with a p.d. of 400 V?
The direction of the force on a current-carrying wire in a magnetic field is given by
items.subtopicHint: Magnetic force on currents and moving charges
items.markingKey: D. Fleming's left-hand rule. Motor effect

items.stem: A 0.5 m wire carrying 4 A lies at right angles to a 0.2 T field. What is the force on it?
items.subtopicHint: Magnetic force on currents and moving charges
items.markingKey: C. 0.4 N. F = BIL

items.stem: Why does a charged particle moving at right angles to a uniform magnetic field travel in a circle?
items.answer: The force is always perpendicular to its velocity
items.subtopicHint: Magnetic force on currents and moving charges
options: The force is along its velocity
The force is always perpendicular to its velocity
items.markingKey: C. The force is always perpendicular to its velocity. It provides centripetal force

items.stem: An e.m.f. is induced in a coil when
items.answer: the magnetic flux through it changes
options: it is stationary in a steady field
the magnetic flux through it changes
items.markingKey: B. the magnetic flux through it changes. Faraday's law

items.stem: Lenz's law states that the induced current
items.answer: opposes the change that produces it
options: opposes the change that produces it
items.markingKey: A. opposes the change that produces it. A consequence of energy conservation

items.stem: The flux through a 100-turn coil falls from 0.03 Wb to 0 in 0.1 s. What is the average induced e.m.f.?
Light behaves as a stream of particles called
items.markingKey: A. photons. Quanta of light

items.stem: In the photoelectric effect, increasing the intensity of light above the threshold frequency increases
options: the maximum kinetic energy of each electron
items.markingKey: A. the number of electrons emitted. More photons per second, same energy each

items.stem: Why does red light fail to eject electrons from zinc even when very bright?
items.answer: Each red photon has less energy than the work function of zinc
options: Each red photon has less energy than the work function of zinc
Red light has too many photons
items.markingKey: A. Each red photon has less energy than the work function of zinc. E = hf is too small

items.stem: What is the concentration of 0.5 mol of NaCl dissolved to make 250 cm³ of solution?
items.markingKey: D. 2 mol/dm³. 0.5 ÷ 0.25 dm³

items.stem: A negative ΔH means the reaction is
items.markingKey: A. exothermic. Heat is released

items.stem: Breaking bonds is
items.markingKey: B. endothermic. Energy is needed to separate atoms

items.stem: At dynamic equilibrium, the rates of the forward and reverse reactions are
items.markingKey: D. equal. Concentrations stay constant

items.stem: For N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃, increasing the pressure shifts the equilibrium
items.answer: to the right, towards fewer gas molecules
options: to the right, towards fewer gas molecules
to the side with more molecules
items.markingKey: A. to the right, towards fewer gas molecules. 4 moles of gas become 2

items.stem: The forward reaction is exothermic. What happens to the yield if the temperature is raised?
items.markingKey: B. It decreases. Equilibrium shifts in the endothermic direction

items.stem: Which molecule is linear?
items.markingKey: B. CO₂. Two bonding domains, no lone pairs

items.stem: Why is water a polar molecule while carbon dioxide is not?
items.answer: Water is bent, so its bond dipoles do not cancel
options: Water is bent, so its bond dipoles do not cancel
Oxygen is less electronegative than hydrogen
CO₂ has lone pairs on carbon
items.markingKey: A. Water is bent, so its bond dipoles do not cancel. Shape decides overall polarity

items.stem: What is the shape of ammonia (NH₃)?
items.markingKey: D. trigonal pyramidal. Three bonding pairs and one lone pair

items.stem: In a galvanic cell, oxidation takes place at the
items.markingKey: A. anode. An Ox, Red Cat

items.stem: What is the role of a salt bridge?
items.answer: It completes the circuit and keeps the solutions electrically neutral
options: It increases the voltage to infinity
It completes the circuit and keeps the solutions electrically neutral
items.markingKey: D. It completes the circuit and keeps the solutions electrically neutral. Ions flow through it

items.stem: E° for Zn²⁺/Zn is -0.76 V and for Cu²⁺/Cu is +0.34 V. What is the cell e.m.f.?
items.markingKey: C. 1.10 V. E°cell = E°cathode - E°anode

items.stem: Which change usually increases the rate of a reaction?
items.markingKey: C. raising the temperature. More successful collisions

items.stem: A catalyst speeds up a reaction by
items.answer: providing a route with lower activation energy
options: providing a route with lower activation energy
items.markingKey: B. providing a route with lower activation energy. Alternative pathway

items.stem: For a first-order reaction, doubling the reactant concentration
items.markingKey: B. doubles the rate. Rate = k[A]

items.stem: Transition metals often form
items.markingKey: D. coloured compounds. Partly filled d subshells

items.stem: Why do transition metals show variable oxidation states?
items.answer: 4s and 3d electrons are close in energy and can both be lost
options: 4s and 3d electrons are close in energy and can both be lost
They have only one valence electron
items.markingKey: A. 4s and 3d electrons are close in energy and can both be lost. Similar energies

items.stem: Why are transition metals and their compounds good catalysts?
items.answer: They can change oxidation state and adsorb reactants on their surface
options: They can change oxidation state and adsorb reactants on their surface
items.markingKey: C. They can change oxidation state and adsorb reactants on their surface. Variable oxidation states

items.stem: A Brønsted-Lowry acid is a
items.markingKey: D. proton donor. It gives H⁺

items.stem: What is the pH of 0.01 mol/dm³ HCl?
items.markingKey: C. 2. pH = -log[H⁺] = -log(10⁻²)

items.stem: A buffer solution
items.answer: resists changes in pH when small amounts of acid or base are added
options: resists changes in pH when small amounts of acid or base are added
items.markingKey: A. resists changes in pH when small amounts of acid or base are added. Weak acid and its conjugate base

items.stem: If f(x) = x² and g(x) = x - 1, what is g(f(3))?
What is the common ratio of 3, 6, 12, 24, ...?
What is the sum to infinity of 8 + 4 + 2 + 1 + ...?
sin²θ + cos²θ =
items.markingKey: D. 1. Pythagorean identity

items.stem: Solve sin x = 0.5 for 0° ≤ x ≤ 360°.
items.markingKey: A. x = 30° or 150°. Sine is positive in the first two quadrants

items.stem: Simplify (1 - cos²θ) / sin θ.
items.markingKey: A. sin θ. 1 - cos²θ = sin²θ

items.stem: How many different 3-letter arrangements can be made from the letters of MATHS (no repeats)?
How many ways can a team of 3 be chosen from 7 players?
What is the term independent of x in (x + 1/x)⁴?
items.markingKey: C. 6. ⁴C₂ x² (1/x)²

items.stem: What is sin⁻¹(1/2) in radians?
cos²θ - sin²θ is equal to
items.markingKey: D. cos 2θ. Double-angle identity

items.stem: What is tan⁻¹(1) + tan⁻¹(√3)?
What is d/dx of (2x + 1)³?
items.markingKey: D. 6(2x + 1)². Chain rule: 3(2x + 1)² x 2

items.stem: What is d/dx of x²·sin x?
items.markingKey: A. 2x sin x + x² cos x. Product rule

items.stem: What is d/dx of eˣ / x?
items.markingKey: C. eˣ(x - 1)/x². Quotient rule

items.stem: ∫ 2x dx =
items.markingKey: A. x² + c. Reverse of differentiation

items.stem: Evaluate ∫₀² 3x² dx.
items.markingKey: B. 8. [x³] from 0 to 2

items.stem: What is the area between y = x² and the x-axis from x = 0 to x = 3?
items.markingKey: C. 9. [x³/3] from 0 to 3

items.stem: What is the magnitude of the vector (3, 4)?
What is the scalar (dot) product of (1, 2, 3) and (4, 0, -1)?
Two non-zero vectors have a dot product of 0. What does this mean?
items.markingKey: C. They are perpendicular. cos 90° = 0

items.stem: In the lock-and-key model, the substrate fits the enzyme's
items.markingKey: A. active site. Complementary shape

items.stem: The cell membrane is mainly made of
items.markingKey: C. a phospholipid bilayer with proteins. Fluid mosaic model

items.stem: Why do small cells exchange materials more efficiently than large cells?
items.answer: They have a larger surface area to volume ratio
options: They have a larger surface area to volume ratio
items.markingKey: C. They have a larger surface area to volume ratio. More surface per unit volume

items.stem: In DNA, adenine pairs with
items.markingKey: B. thymine. Complementary base pairing

items.stem: Which molecule carries the genetic code from the nucleus to the ribosome?
items.markingKey: D. mRNA. Transcription

items.stem: A DNA strand reads ATG CCA. What is the complementary mRNA?
items.markingKey: D. UAC GGU. U replaces T in RNA

items.stem: Gas exchange in the lungs happens in the
items.markingKey: B. alveoli. Thin walls, large surface

items.stem: Haemoglobin carries
items.markingKey: A. oxygen. In red blood cells

items.stem: Why does carbon monoxide poisoning cause tissues to lack oxygen?
items.answer: CO binds to haemoglobin more strongly than oxygen
options: CO binds to haemoglobin more strongly than oxygen
items.markingKey: C. CO binds to haemoglobin more strongly than oxygen. Less haemoglobin is free for O₂

items.stem: ATP is
items.answer: the energy currency of the cell
options: the energy currency of the cell
items.markingKey: A. the energy currency of the cell. Adenosine triphosphate

items.stem: Where does the Krebs cycle take place?
items.markingKey: D. mitochondrial matrix. Glycolysis is in the cytoplasm

items.stem: Why is oxygen called the final electron acceptor?
items.answer: It accepts electrons at the end of the electron transport chain, forming water
options: It accepts electrons at the end of the electron transport chain, forming water
items.markingKey: D. It accepts electrons at the end of the electron transport chain, forming water. Without it the chain stops

items.stem: The light-dependent reactions of photosynthesis take place in the
items.markingKey: C. thylakoid membranes. Where chlorophyll is

items.stem: Which gas is released by the splitting of water (photolysis)?
items.markingKey: C. oxygen. Water → H⁺ + e⁻ + O₂

items.stem: Why does the rate of photosynthesis stop increasing at high light intensity?
items.answer: Another factor, such as CO₂ or temperature, becomes limiting
options: Another factor, such as CO₂ or temperature, becomes limiting
Plants close all stomata at once
items.markingKey: B. Another factor, such as CO₂ or temperature, becomes limiting. Limiting factors

items.stem: Maintaining a constant internal environment is called
items.markingKey: A. homeostasis. Steady state

items.stem: Which hormone lowers blood glucose?
items.markingKey: D. insulin. From beta cells of the pancreas

items.stem: Negative feedback works by
items.answer: reversing a change to bring a variable back to its set point
options: reversing a change to bring a variable back to its set point
items.markingKey: A. reversing a change to bring a variable back to its set point. Corrective response

items.stem: Charles Darwin proposed the theory of
items.markingKey: B. evolution by natural selection. On the Origin of Species

items.stem: Selection that favours one extreme of a range of phenotypes is
items.markingKey: B. directional selection. The mean shifts

items.stem: Two populations of a species are separated by a mountain range for thousands of years. What may happen?
items.answer: They may become separate species through allopatric speciation
options: They may become separate species through allopatric speciation
items.markingKey: C. They may become separate species through allopatric speciation. Geographical isolation

items.stem: What number comes next? 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, ?
items.explanation: Each term is the sum of the two before it

items.stem: Money doubles in 6 years at a fixed compound rate. In how many years does it become 8 times?
Boys and girls in a class are in the ratio 3 : 5. After 6 more boys join, the ratio is 1 : 1. How many students were there at first?
One pipe fills a tank in 6 hours; another empties it in 9 hours. If both are open, how long does it take to fill the empty tank?
Which phrase is closest in meaning to 'ubiquitous'?
Author is to novel as composer is to ...
Some economists are writers. All writers are readers. Which statement must be true?
items.explanation: The economists who are writers are also readers

items.stem: Claim: 'Since the new study app launched, the school's test scores rose, so the app raised scores.' Which fact, if true, most weakens the claim?
options: The school also hired extra teachers at the same time
Students said they liked the app
items.answer: The school also hired extra teachers at the same time
items.explanation: Another change at the same time offers a different explanation

items.stem: What comes next? AZ, BY, CX, ?
items.explanation: First letters go forward, second letters go backward

items.stem: What comes next? 1, 2, 6, 24, 120, ?
Figures: shaded triangle, unshaded square, shaded pentagon, ... Each figure gains one side and the shading alternates. What is the next figure?
items.explanation: Six sides, and the shading switches back to unshaded

items.stem: What is the smaller angle between the hour and minute hands of a clock at 3:15?
items.explanation: The hour hand has moved a quarter of 30° past the 3

items.stem: From home you walk 4 km north and then 3 km east. How far are you from home in a straight line?
A 3 x 3 x 3 cube is painted on all faces and cut into 27 small cubes. How many small cubes have exactly one painted face?
items.explanation: One at the centre of each face
